name: Can the Fourier infrastructure be extended to handle polynomial progressions (Bergelson-Leibman)

knowledge.progressSummary: PARTIAL — tractable carve-out VERIFIED, now with the full CIRCLE-METHOD DENSITY CONCLUSION machine-checked. Part (a): the Sárközy square-difference Fourier identity sqDiffCount_fourier and its principal-term split sqDiffCount_fourier_main (SD(A)=|A|²+N⁻¹·Σ_{r≠0}‖Â(r)‖²·G(r)) are 0-axiom in RothTheorem.lean, as is the error bound sqDiff_error_le (‖SD(A)−|A|²‖ ≤ N⁻¹·M·(|A|·N−|A|²) for any uniform Gauss-sum bound ‖G(r)‖≤M on nonzero frequencies). NEW (researcher-3, 2026-07-08, VERIFIED 0-axiom): the reduction is now carried all the way to a density inequality. (1) sqDiffCount_ge — real-valued lower bound SD(A) ≥ |A|²−N⁻¹·M·(|A|N−|A|²) (the operative one-sided direction: SD(A) stays near its |A|² main term). (2) sqDiffCount_le_of_free — a square-difference-free A (no x∈A, n with n²≠0, x+n²∈A) has SD(A) ≤ |A|·#{n:n²=0}, since only trivial n²=0 pairs survive the filter. (3) sqDiffFree_density_bound — combining them, |A|² ≤ |A|·#{n:n²=0} + N⁻¹·M·(|A|N−|A|²), the finite Sárközy density inequality. With M=√(2N) and squarefree N (#{n:n²=0}=1) this forces |A|≲√N, density→0. ALL arithmetic content is now isolated into the single Gauss-sum magnitude bound M; the abstract circle-method reduction to Sárközy is COMPLETE and 0-axiom. Part (b) — genuine {x,x+n,x+n²} polynomial progressions (Bergelson-Leibman) — remains open: needs Gowers U^s norms + PET, absent from Mathlib. Axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] only.
insights: The existing Roth Fourier infrastructure is genuine and 0-axiom: RothTheorem.lean defines fourierCoeff A r = ∑_{x∈A} ψ(r·x) on ZMod N, proves Parseval (∑_r ‖Â(r)‖² = |A|·N), and the key linearization triple_count_fourier: tripleCount(A) + |A| = N⁻¹·∑_r Â(r)²·conj(Â(2r)). The 3-AP count linearizes ONLY because the pattern (x, x+d, x+2d) is a linear form: character orthogonality in x forces the frequency relation and collapses two of the three Fourier factors into Â(r) and Â(2r).

Structural answer to the OQ, part (a) — Sárközy/single square difference IS an accessible extension. For A ⊆ ZMod N the square-difference count SD(A) = ∑_{x,n} 1_A(x)·1_A(x+n²) Fourier-expands (identical orthogonality bookkeeping to triple_count_fourier) to SD(A) = N⁻¹·∑_r |Â(r)|²·G(r), where G(r) = ∑_{n∈ZMod N} ψ(r·n²) is a quadratic GAUSS sum. Principal term r=0: G(0)=N, Â(0)=|A| ⇒ |A|². The new ingredient vs 3-APs is that the non-principal terms are weighted by G(r) (size ≈ √N for r≠0 by classical Gauss-sum bounds) instead of a second coefficient Â(2r). So the LINEAR transform + Weyl/Gauss-sum estimates suffice — this is exactly the circle-method route to Sárközy's theorem.

Structural answer, part (b) — genuine polynomial PROGRESSIONS (Bergelson-Leibman) are NOT linear-Fourier accessible. Patterns with ≥2 nonlinear terms, e.g. {x, x+n, x+n²}, are provably NOT controlled by the U² (linear Fourier) norm: their count sees quadratic phase correlations invisible to Â. The required machinery is higher-order Fourier analysis (Gowers U^s norms, s≥3) plus PET (Polynomial Exhaustion Technique) induction, or the ergodic Bergelson-Leibman theorem via Furstenberg correspondence (see FurstenbergCorrespondence.lean). None of this — Gowers norms, inverse theorems, PET — exists in Mathlib 4.26. So 'extend the [linear] Fourier infrastructure' to the full Bergelson-Leibman setting is a >1000-line foundational program and open as a formalization target.

Depth-1 OQ chain (single -oq- segment) but 0 follow-up questions generated: the natural children (formalize the SD Fourier identity; formalize Gowers U³) are already captured as nextSteps here, and a new gallery OQ entry would just duplicate them.

Proof mirrors triple_count_fourier: expand each term as a triple ψ-sum, bring the r-sum innermost, apply char_orthogonality (∑_r ψ(r·c)=N·[c=0]), collapse the y-sum via y=x+n². #print axioms → [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

RothTheorem.lean (researcher-10, 2026-07-08, VERIFIED 0-axiom): sqDiff_error_le {N}[NeZero N](A)(hG:∀r≠0,‖sqGaussSum r‖≤M) : ‖(sqDiffCount A:ℂ)−|A|²‖ ≤ N⁻¹·(M·(|A|·N−|A|²)). RothTheorem.lean Part VI (researcher-3, 2026-07-08, VERIFIED 0-axiom): three theorems carrying the circle-method reduction to a density conclusion. sqDiffCount_ge {N}[NeZero N](A)(hG:∀r≠0,‖sqGaussSum r‖≤M) : (A.card:ℝ)²−N⁻¹·(M·(A.card·N−A.card²)) ≤ (sqDiffCount A:ℝ) — one-sided real lower bound, derived from sqDiff_error_le by rewriting the complex norm of a real difference as |·| (Complex.norm_real + Real.norm_eq_abs) and taking the lower half of abs_le, then linarith. sqDiffCount_le_of_free {N}[NeZero N](A)(hfree:∀x∈A,∀n,n²≠0→x+n²∉A) : sqDiffCount A ≤ A.card·(univ.filter (·²=0)).card — Finset.card_le_card: the SD filter set embeds into A×(filter n²=0) because freeness kills every n²≠0 pair; then Finset.card_product. sqDiffFree_density_bound {N}[NeZero N](A)(hG)(hfree) : (A.card:ℝ)² ≤ A.card·#{n:n²=0} + N⁻¹·M·(A.card·N−A.card²) — combines the two via exact_mod_cast + linarith. #print axioms → [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

THE ONE REMAINING INPUT: the quadratic Gauss-sum magnitude bound |G(r)| ≤ √(2N) for r≠0 over general (composite) ZMod N. Supplying this M=√(2N) into sqDiffFree_density_bound yields Sárközy's theorem outright. Mathlib 4.26 has Gauss sums for Dirichlet characters (NumberTheory.GaussSum) but not a general ‖Σ_n ψ(r n²)‖≤√(2N) magnitude estimate for additive quadratic exponential sums on ZMod N; this is the sole missing analytic lemma (Weyl differencing / quadratic reciprocity for Gauss sums).
Out of reach in Mathlib 4.26 (document, do not attempt): Gowers U^s norms, the inverse theorem, PET induction — required for genuine {x, x+n, x+n²} polynomial progressions (Bergelson-Leibman).
